panels.bubble_text: Every one stood on the shoulders of those before.
panels.speaker: VELVET

panels.text: Here they are. The builders of the computing stack, in the order they appear in our story. Notice how each generation inherits what the previous generation built — and then extends it one layer higher.

panels.prompt: A striking black-and-white photograph-style illustration of six women in 1940s clothing standing at a massive room-sized computer covered in cables and switches, their faces determined and focused, but the photograph is slightly faded at the edges as if being forgotten — one corner peels away revealing glowing warm color beneath, symbolizing their work enduring despite being erased from history. Comic book style, warm editorial illustration with ink lines and watercolor washes, sepia tones with warm orange accent on the peeling corner

panels.text:
Notice who is missing from the fame. The six women who programmed ENIAC were erased from photographs and forgotten for decades. Tommy Flowers spent his own money building Colossus, then was silenced by the Official Secrets Act. Konrad Zuse built the Z3 in his parents' living room — and it was destroyed in a bombing raid.

History is not always fair. But their work endured.
That was the first half of the timeline — from theory to networking. Now let's see the modern era: from free software to agent swarms.
